title: Play Therapy Techniques
tagline: Play is the child's language; toys are the words.
welcome: Children do not sit and talk; they play and show. This course teaches you to enter their world fluently and therapeutically.
vignette: A six-year-old buries the baby doll in the sand tray, uncovers it, and buries it again, three times. Then she looks up, not for permission, but for a witness. The play therapist understands: something has been said, and heard.
vignette_attr: A sandtray moment, drawn from supervised practice
description: A comprehensive training in play therapy: its history and major models, the therapeutic powers of play, child-centered play therapy skills, directive and expressive techniques, sandtray and art-based methods, limit-setting, and tracking across a course of treatment.
questions: What is the child saying through play?
When do I follow and when do I lead?
How do I hold safety and freedom in one room?
importance: Play is developmentally the child's natural medium of expression
Evidence supports play therapy for trauma, anxiety, and behavior
Without play skills, a counselor is partly blind with children
misconceptions: that play therapy is just playing, when it is a disciplined clinical method
that it is only for little children, when play and expressive methods reach adolescents too
figures: whose child-centered principles defined the field
who systematized child-centered play therapy training
who named the therapeutic powers of play
outcomes: Apply the major play therapy models
You will distinguish and use child-centered and directive approaches.
You will track, reflect, and return responsibility with fluency.
You will select structured interventions matched to the child.
You will hold a symbolic process with skill and restraint.
You will hold safety without shaming the child.
Track and document a course of treatment
You will record play themes and progress across sessions.
modules: History and Models of Play Therapy
Knowing the models keeps your choices deliberate.
The powers explain why the method works.
These skills are the bedrock of the room.
Directive tools target what the child brings.
Symbolic methods reach pre-verbal and buried material.
Safety and freedom share the same room.
Treatment is a journey, not an event.
assessment: Assessment is performance and portfolio based.
tips: Practice tracking until it is effortless
Let the child lead more than feels comfortable
Hold the parent as an ally of the play
integration: Play therapy is the signature clinical method for children in this programme.
faith: We enter the child's world with the reverence of a guest, honoring play as their sacred language.
closing: May you learn the child's language so well that no child is left without words.
